##### **1.2 Structural Architecture of a C Source Program** The structural architecture of a C source translation unit is organized into six formal, sequential divisions: the **documentation section**, the **link section**, the **definition section**, the **global declaration section**, the **`main()` function section**, and the **subprogram section**. * **Documentation section**: Contains high-level commentary, such as the program description, author identity, and copyright notices. * **Link section**: Supplies preprocessor directives (such as `#include `) directing the compiler to link required library declarations and external interface headers. * **Definition section**: Declares symbolic constants and functional macros using preprocessor directives such as `#define PI 3.1415926`. * **Global declaration section**: Houses global variable definitions and function prototypes that remain visible and accessible across multiple functions. * **`main()` function section**: Defines the mandated primary execution entry point called when the program launches. It contains two internal components: * **Declaration part**: Specifies all local variables, allocate-on-stack identifiers, and types utilized by the function. * **Executable part**: Contains runtime statements, computation instructions, input/output calls, and return operations. * **Subprogram section**: Contains the operational definitions for all user-defined functions invoked across the translation unit. Every valid C executable program strictly requires exactly one **`main()` function section**. All remaining five sections are entirely optional according to the language specification; a minimal legal program consists solely of an empty or returning `main()` definition. ```{mermaid} %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'Helvetica', 'primaryColor': '#e8f4f8', 'primaryTextColor': '#1f2d3d', 'primaryBorderColor': '#355c7d', 'lineColor': '#355c7d', 'secondaryColor': '#d6eef5', 'tertiaryColor': '#fff3cd', 'background': '#ffffff', 'mainBkg': '#e8f4f8', 'secondBkg': '#d6eef5', 'tertiaryBkg': '#fff3cd', 'clusterBkg': '#f9fbfd', 'clusterBorder': '#355c7d', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff' }}}%% %%| fig-cap: "Structural architecture and section dependencies of a standard C source translation unit." %%| fig-width: 7 %%| fig-height: 4 flowchart TB subgraph OptionalSections["Optional Pre-Execution Context"] A["Documentation Section
(Program notes, author)"] B["Link Section
(#include directives)"] C["Definition Section
(#define macros, constants)"] D["Global Declaration Section
(Global variables, prototypes)"] end subgraph MandatorySection["Mandatory Entry Point"] E["main() Function Section"] E1["Declaration Part
(Local variable declarations)"] E2["Executable Part
(Computations, returns)"] E --> E1 E --> E2 end subgraph AuxiliarySection["Auxiliary Code"] F["Subprogram Section
(User-defined functions)"] end A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F ``` The concrete arrangement of these six structural divisions within a single source file appears as follows: ```c // Documentation section // Author: Operating Systems Sample #include // Link section #define PI 3.1415926 // Definition section int global_var; // Global declaration section void compute(void); // Global declaration section (prototype) int main(void) // main() function section { int local_var; // Declaration part local_var = 10; // Executable part compute(); // Executable part return 0; // Executable part } void compute(void) // Subprogram section { global_var = 1; } ```
